newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firmer on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firmer on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was firmer against the dollar on the back of tight money market liquidity in early trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said tight liquidity forced many domestic operators to unload dollars to meet rupiah demand.
Spot rupiah rose to 2,595/97 at 0220 GMT from 2,600/05 at the opening. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,594.5/96.5 and 2,593.5/95.5 respectively.
"Sentiment on the rupiah seems to improve, in line with a more settled market in Thailand," one U.S. bank dealer said.

He said Thailand seemed to hold the key for a recovery in the region. "Thailand is the locomotive for now. If the package agreed with the IMF could regain market confidence, I think we are going to see a broad recovery throughout the region."
Thailand was holding a meeting with IMF to work out a package to revive its ailing economy. A final agreement is expected to be submitted for cabinet approval on Tuesday.
One local bank dealer said increased rupiah demand in the early morning also partly resulted from higher spot dollar purchases on Friday which were maturing on Tuesday.
She said the central bank was likely to extend the tight grip on the rupiah in the short-term until the foreign exchange market showed signs of stabilisation.
Dealers said money market and swap rates appeared to move more in line after recent attractive arbitrage opportunity.
Overnight swap was at 1.0/1.2 and tom/next at 0.55/0.65. Overnight money cooled down to 20.0 percent from 27.0 percent.
Dealers said focus was also on the swap market after Malaysia imposed restrictions on swap trading without underlying trade-related transactions.

"I don't know whether Bank Indonesia has a similar plan or not. But I think it's unlikely that Bank Indonesia would copy such a step because it would be a setback in its liberalisation efforts," the U.S. bank dealer said.

"The central bank would do that if there is an emergency. I don't see such an emergency for now. Instead, the market appears to be on a recovery path," the dealer said, adding that rates were hovering within the central bank range.
The central bank said earlier dollar-rupiah between 2,555 and 2,610 ranges was normal under current conditions.
Dealers said while the short-dated swaps were determined by money market liquidity, the longer-term swaps were kept biddish following the Malaysian move to control swap trading.
One-month swap was at 22.0/25.0, two at 41.0/47.0, three at 60.0/65.0 and six at 124.0/129.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,580/2,628 on Monday from 2,585/2,633 on Friday.
